messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: New feature: add_dataframe
parts:
Hi all,

I'm happy to announce a new feature that, judging by the questions
I've been responding lately, will be well-received by many of you. It
aims to meet the need to attach preexistent (or precomputed) data with
attributes.

Until now, this was possible by passing the arrival times to the
add_generator method and then cleverly consuming other attributes
directly in the trajectory (I shared here and on StackOverflow a
function called "consume" for this).

Instead, the new add_dataframe enables the following:

lambda <- 1
mu <- 2

customer_data <- data.frame(
time = rexp(1000 * lambda, lambda),
service = rexp(1000 * mu, mu)
)

customer <- trajectory() %>%
seize("clerk") %>%
timeout_from_attribute("service") %>%
release("clerk")

env <- simmer() %>%
add_resource("clerk", 1) %>%
add_dataframe("customer", customer, customer_data) %>%
run()

which is not only convenient, but very fast. I encourage you all to
try this new feature. It can be tested by installing the feature-data
branch with remotes (or devtools):

remotes::install_github("r-simmer/simmer", ref="feature-data")

Don't forget to read the help page (?add_dataframe), because it has
many arguments to pick the right columns. It still needs some testing,
but I think it will be more than ready for the next release (on May).
Any feedback would be very welcome.

Regards,
Iñaki
